reimscathedral.name: Reims Cathedral
reimscathedral.slogan: Where France crowned its kings, and a stone angel still smiles.
reimscathedral.line: Clovis was baptised on this site around 496, and French kings were crowned here until Charles X in 1825.

pommerycellars.name: Pommery Cellars
pommerycellars.slogan: Down the stairs into Madame Pommery's chalk cathedral of bottles.
pommerycellars.line: Widowed in 1860, Louise Pommery took over the house and made the first brut champagne, with no added sugar.

reddition.name: Surrender Museum
reddition.slogan: A school classroom where a continent finally exhaled.
reddition.line: At 2:41 a.m. on 7 May 1945, Germany signed its surrender in a red-brick Reims schoolhouse, headquarters of Allied command.

moetchandon.name: Moët & Chandon
moetchandon.slogan: Cellars and chandeliers on Épernay's avenue of champagne.
moetchandon.line: Founded in 1743 by Claude Moët, a wine trader from Épernay.

hautvillersabbey.name: Hautvillers Abbey
hautvillersabbey.slogan: The hillside village where a monk gave champagne its bubbles.
hautvillersabbey.line: Its vineyards, presses and cellars joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2015 as the Champagne hillsides, houses and cellars.
